title: What is known about 1RB0LA_1LC1RF_---1LD_1RE0LA_1RA0RB_1RE0RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LA_1LC1RF_---1LD_1RE0LA_1RA0RB_1RE0RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. It behaves like a slow unary counter: the tape starts with a run of copies of 110, and on every return to the left end that run is exactly one copy longer. Behind the run sits a second run of 110 and a short, disordered stretch at the right end, and that stretch is where the open question lives.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps. The C simulator shows, up to 109 steps, 671 returns to the left end, at each of which the counter p has grown by exactly 1 (from 2 at step 52 to 672 at step 997,776,132). What the right end does is not understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: Two shift rules
claims.text: The rightward sweep E> (110)^n becomes (011)^n E> in 3n steps, and the leftward zigzag (011)^n A> 0 0 becomes A> 0 0 (011)^n in 5n steps (the run of words moves 3 cells right past the gap).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,948 cells have been visited and 2,621 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The counter
claims.text: Every time up to 109 steps that the head is at the left end in A on A>0 0, the tape is 0 0 (110)^p followed by the rest. There are 671 such times; p is 2 at step 52 and 672 at step 997,776,132, and it goes up by exactly 1 each time.
claims.where: py/counter.py on a tmrun … at A L log

claims.title: Cost of a round
claims.text: The number of steps between returns, divided by p², is 10.06–10.1 for the last five rounds. Summing 10·p² over rounds gives t ≈ 3.4·p³, i.e. p ≈ 670 at 10<sup>9</sup> steps, as seen.

claims.title: What follows the counter
claims.text: Right after (110)^p comes 0 0 0 when p ≡ 0 or 2 (mod 3) and 0 1 1 when p ≡ 1 (mod 3), at all 601 returns after step 106. Then comes a second run (110)^q (q = 629 for the last returns, about 0.9·p), then 20–30 disordered cells, e.g. 0^4 (110)^3 0^8 110 0^2 10 0 110 0^2 1 at step 997,776,132.

claims.title: Width
claims.text: From one return to the next the width grows by 6 cells in 556 of 670 rounds (other values 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 10, 14); it is 3,943 at step 997,776,132.

claims.title: Not every run of 1s is even
claims.text: Odd runs of 1s (lengths 1, 3, 5) occur far from the head, in every state and on both sides (a scan of every 13th step up to step 400,000), and the disordered end at the 667 returns to the left end takes 658 different shapes of 3 to 50 cells. So the even-run property holds only for the runs E reaches; an invariant has to say where the odd runs can be.

claims.title: How near it comes to halting
claims.text: In the first 109 steps E reads a 1 123,762,963 times with exactly two 1s from the head (E>1 1 0) and 429,985 times with four (E>1 1 1 1 0); never with one, which is what a halt needs. So the disordered right end never puts E on a lone 1 either: E's runs of 1s are always of even length.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.325). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.333).

claims.title: No closed tape language found
claims.text: Closed-language searches all fail: windows of up to 8 cells grown as needed (also with flags for run parity, odd runs seen, position mod 3) leave thousands of halting abstract configurations (9,071 at 8 cells with run parity). The shortest abstract path to a halt (45 steps, 8 cells) goes wrong when the tape first outgrows the window: from C>1 1 1 1 0 0 1 1, 9 cells, the window forgets where blank tape starts. DFAs learned from the run (k-tails with folding) with the least NFA on the other side fail too.

claims.title: No small automaton proof
claims.text: A finite-automata-reduction search (DFA on one side, least NFA on the other; far.c in 1RB0LA_0RC---_0RD0RF_1LD0LE_0LA1LE_0RA0LA) finds no certificate with up to 7 DFA states on the left or 8 on the right, and there is no conserved quantity a·ones + b·position + W[state] modulo 2 to 12.

claims.title: How it could halt
claims.text: The halting transition is C reading 0. C is entered only from B reading 0 (which writes 1 and moves left), and B is entered from A on 0 (which leaves a 1 to B's left) or from E on 1 (which leaves a 0). So a halt is exactly E>1 0: E on a 1 with a 0 to its right. It has not happened in 109 steps.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The counter steps by 1 at every one of the 670 rounds seen, and E never meets a lone 1 in 10<sup>9</sup> steps (its runs of 1s are always even); why, and why the disordered right end keeps it so, are open.

check: gcc -O2 -o tmrun tools/c/tmrun.c && ./tmrun 1RB0LA_1LC1RF_---1LD_1RE0LA_1RA0RB_1RE0RF 1000000000 at A L 100000 > al.txt && python3 holdouts/1RB0LA_1LC1RF_---1LD_1RE0LA_1RA0RB_1RE0RF/py/counter.py al.txt

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The machine is a counter: at every return to the left end the tape begins (110)^p, with p one more than last time. A round costs about 10·p² steps, so after t steps p is about (0.3·t)1/3, and the width (about 6 cells more per round) follows the same law. The right end is a short disordered stretch the machine never halts in, so far.

facts.text: Returns to the left end, up to 10<sup>9</sup> steps, at which p went up by exactly 1.
Steps from one return to the next (10.06 to 10.1 over the last five).
Growth of p and of the width: p = 672, width 3,943 at step 997,776,132.

sections.heading: A counter made of 110s
html: Stop the machine whenever it is at the left end of the tape in state A, reading A>0 0. Written with c = 110, the tapes at the last four such times are:

The first run of 110s is the counter p. It goes up by exactly one per round, 670 times in a row from p = 2 at step 52. Between returns the head walks the whole tape, and inside the run it moves by a back-and-forth (states B and C) that converts one 110 per 5 steps; a round costs about 10·p² steps.
After the counter come 0 0 0, or 0 1 1 when p ≡ 1 mod 3,, a second run (110)^q that grows only now and then (q = 629 for the last returns), and a short disordered stretch at the right end.

sections.heading: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
html: Round p costs about 10·p² steps and adds one to p, so after p rounds about 10·p³/3 steps have passed: p ≈ (0.3·t)1/3, which is 670 at 109 steps (672 seen). The width grows by about 6 cells a round (6 in 556 of 670 rounds), so it grows the same way: 3,943 cells at step 997,776,132.
The machine halts only if E reads a 1 with a 0 to its right, which would have to happen in the disordered stretch.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.325). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.333).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,948 cells (1,097 left of the start, 2,106 right), with a density of 1s of 0.664.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: counter of 110 blocks with a messy right end
summary: Each time the head is back at the left end the tape starts with (110)^p, and p has gone up by exactly 1 since the last time; a round costs about 10·p² steps, so p and the width grow like t^(1/3).
